sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.3890 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and Command Area Development appearing for respondent No.1, learned Government Pleader for Finance and Planning for the respondent No.2 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondent Nos.3 and 4.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed seeking a writ of Mandamus to declare the action of the respondents in not paying the compensation amounts to the petitioners as per Judgment and Decree of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Hanamkonda, in L.A.O.P.No.128 of 2013, dated 26.06.2023 as arbitrary and illegal.

3. It is the case of the petitioners herein that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of their respective houses situated at Gaigollapaly Village, SK,J Kusumanchi Mandal and their houses were acquired of submergence in Singoor Project in pursuance to the draft notification under Section 4(1)
and draft declaration of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Aggrieved by the compensation fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the petitioners filed L.A.O.P.No.128 of 2013 on the file of Principle Senior Civil Judge, Hanamkonda wherein the compensation was enhanced from Rs.80,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/- per acre.

As the respondents failed to deposit the compensation amount, the petitioner filed E.P.No.119 of 2023 in L.A.O.P.No.128 of 2013 on the file of Principle Senior Civil Judge, Hanamkonda and the petitioners approached this Court by filing the present Writ Petition seeking a direction to the respondents to deposit the amount into the credit of E.P.No.119 of 2023.

4. Having regard to the above backdrop of the case, this Court is of the considered view that the authorities cannot take their own time to deposit the enhanced compensation amount payable to the petitioners.

The inaction of the SK,J respondents in not paying the enhanced compensation amounts to the petitioners, who were already suffered by losing their houses and made them to suffer untold hardship and misery to run from pillar to post for getting the enhanced compensation,
for which they also incurred expenses.
Apart from that the petitioners have also to incur additional expenditure for approaching the Court for seeking the required relief.

With the raising inflation, the value of the money will also go down and the delayed payment of the enhanced compensation will result in the compensation amount itself losing all the charm and utility.

If the petitioners or similarly situated persons receive the enhanced compensation within the time, they will be in a position to use that amount in some other investments and would get some returns over the same.

5. Having regard to the same, the Writ Petition is disposed of and the respondents are directed to deposit the amount in terms of the order and decree, dated 26.06.2023, passed in L.A.O.P.No.128 of 2013 on the file of SK,J the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Hanamkonda to the credit of E.P.No.119 of 2023 in L.A.O.P.No.128 of 2013 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Hanamkonda, as Bhukya Nagu vs State Of Telangana on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141595796/
